    10	
    11	/-!
    12	# The Abel inverse of the canonical evaluation divisor, unconditionally
    13	
    14	`rankOneDivisorUniqueness` (`Pic0RankOneUniquenessDischarge.lean`) settles, over every affine
    15	test whose plus class lies in the rank-one locus, that at most one widened locally certified
    16	divisor class of degree `genus C` has a prescribed Abel value.  This file upgrades that affine
    17	statement into the second inverse law of the rank-one Abel/evaluation pair on the big site: every
    18	`E : PicRankOneEvaluationDivisorData pi` automatically satisfies `E.AbelInverse`, so its
    19	`evaluationIso` is available with no extra hypothesis.
    20	
    21	The upgrade is genuinely local-to-global on the base, and it reuses only landed material:
    22	
    23	* **The vehicle collapse along an affine open** (`divFamZarAffAffineEquiv_map_fromSpecAffine`):
    24	  restricting a widened vehicle section along `Over.fromSpecAffine T U` and collapsing through the
    25	  affine comparison recovers the section's value at the affine open `U`.  This is the `mapVal`
    26	  no-gluing computation followed by the `Spec`-`Γ` bookkeeping identity
    27	  `fromSpecAffine_ΓTop_comp_appLEAlgHom`.
    28	* **Arbitrary-test uniqueness** (`divFamZarAff_eq_of_rankOne`): two widened vehicle sections over
    29	  an arbitrary test whose Abel values agree, one of whose Abel classes lies in the rank-one locus,
    30	  are equal.  Two sections of the widened vehicle agree iff they agree on affine opens
    31	  (`divFamZarAff.ext`); on each affine open the pulled-back rank-one class (via
    32	  `picRankOneOpen_map_mem` along `Over.fromSpecAffine T U`) feeds the affine
    33	  `rankOneDivisorUniqueness`, with the affine Abel value identified through
    34	  `picEtMap_abelDivAff'`, `picEtAffineEquiv_abelDivAff'`, and the vehicle collapse above.
    35	* **Monomorphy of the restricted Abel map** (`rankOneAbelSigma_app_injective`): arbitrary-test
    36	  uniqueness gives injectivity of the represented Abel map on every slice object, and the
    37	  `Σ`-extension preserves it componentwise.
    38	
    39	Given a right inverse (`E.divisor_abel`) and injectivity of `rankOneAbelSigma pi`, the standard
    40	cancellation yields the left inverse `E.AbelInverse`, hence the packaged `rankOneAbelIso`.
    41	-/
    42	
    43	set_option autoImplicit false
    44	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
    45	/- `lake env lean` drops the lakefile's `[leanOptions]` (I-0161), so the pinned synthesis
    46	depth must be set in-file for the faithful per-file check. -/
    47	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    48	
    49	universe u
    50	
    51	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
    52	
    53	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    54	
    55	attribute [local instance] Over.sectionsAlgebra Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    56	
    57	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    58	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    59	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    60	variable (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi]
    61	
    62	noncomputable section
    63	
    64	/-! ## The vehicle collapse along an affine open -/
    65	
    66	omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] in
    67	/-- Restricting a widened vehicle section along the affine-open test object `Over.fromSpecAffine
    68	T U` and collapsing through the affine comparison recovers the section's value at `U`.  The
    69	`mapVal` no-gluing computation and the `Spec`-`Γ` bookkeeping identity
    70	`fromSpecAffine_ΓTop_comp_appLEAlgHom`. -/
    71	theorem divFamZarAffAffineEquiv_map_fromSpecAffine (n : ℕ) (T : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    72	    (s : divFamZarAff C n T) (U : T.left.affineOpens) :
    73	    divFamZarAffAffineEquiv C n Γ(T.left, U.1)
    74	        (divFamZarAff.map C n (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) s)
    75	      = s.1 U := by
    76	  rw [divFamZarAffAffineEquiv_apply, divFamZarAff.map_val,
    77	    divFamZarAff.mapVal_eq_mapAlgHom C n (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) s
    78	      (top_le_preimage_fromSpecAffine T U),
    79	    ← DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom_comp, fromSpecAffine_ΓTop_comp_appLEAlgHom T U,
    80	    DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom_id]
    81	
    82	/-! ## Arbitrary-test uniqueness of the widened Abel map on the rank-one locus -/
    83	
    84	/-- **Arbitrary-test rank-one uniqueness**: two widened vehicle sections over an arbitrary test
    85	`T` whose widened Abel values agree, one of whose Abel classes lies in the rank-one locus, are
    86	equal.  The vehicle is separated by affine opens, and on each affine open the pulled-back rank-one
    87	class feeds the affine `rankOneDivisorUniqueness`. -/
    88	theorem divFamZarAff_eq_of_rankOne (T : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    89	    (s₁ s₂ : divFamZarAff C (genus C) T)
    90	    (hs₁ : (abelDivAffTrans C (genus C)).app (op T) s₁ ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj (op T))
    91	    (habel : abelDivAff' C (genus C) T s₁ = abelDivAff' C (genus C) T s₂) :
    92	    s₁ = s₂ := by
    93	  refine divFamZarAff.ext fun U => ?_
    94	  -- pull the rank-one class back along the affine-open test object
    95	  have hmem : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map (Over.fromSpecAffine T U).op
    96	        ((abelDivAffTrans C (genus C)).app (op T) s₁)
    97	      ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj (op (overSpec k Γ(T.left, U.1))) :=
    98	    picRankOneOpen_map_mem pi (Over.fromSpecAffine T U).op hs₁
    99	  -- the pulled-back Abel value is the affine Abel value of `s₁.1 U`
   100	  have hval : abelDivAffPlus C Γ(T.left, U.1) (s₁.1 U)
   101	      = picEtAffineEquiv C Γ(T.left, U.1)
   102	          ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map (Over.fromSpecAffine T U).op
   103	            ((abelDivAffTrans C (genus C)).app (op T) s₁)).1 := by
   104	    have h1 : ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map (Over.fromSpecAffine T U).op
   105	          ((abelDivAffTrans C (genus C)).app (op T) s₁)).1
   106	        = picEtMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) (abelDivAff' C (genus C) T s₁) := rfl
   107	    rw [h1, picEtMap_abelDivAff', picEtAffineEquiv_abelDivAff',
   108	      divFamZarAffAffineEquiv_map_fromSpecAffine]
   109	  -- the two affine Abel values agree, from equality of the vehicle Abel values
   110	  have hU := congrArg (fun w : picEt C T => w.1 U) habel
   111	  rw [abelDivAff'_val, abelDivAff'_val] at hU
   112	  exact rankOneDivisorUniqueness pi Γ(T.left, U.1) _ hmem (s₁.1 U) (s₂.1 U) hval
   113	    (hU.symm.trans hval)
   114	
   115	/-! ## Monomorphy of the restricted Abel map -/
   116	
   117	/-- The represented Abel map is injective on every slice object: this is arbitrary-test
   118	uniqueness read through the subfunctor preimage plumbing. -/
   119	theorem rankOneAbelRepresented_app_injective (Z : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
   120	    Function.Injective ((rankOneAbelRepresented pi).app (op Z)) := by
   121	  intro x y h
   122	  have hinj : Function.Injective
   123	      ((divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).toIso.hom.app (op Z)) :=
   124	    Function.LeftInverse.injective fun a =>
   125	      (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).toIso.hom_inv_id_app_apply (op Z) a
   126	  set sx := (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).toIso.hom.app (op Z) x.val with hsx
   127	  set sy := (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).toIso.hom.app (op Z) y.val with hsy
   128	  -- the underlying widened Abel values agree
   129	  have happ : ∀ w : (divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi).toFunctor.obj (op Z),
   130	      ((rankOneAbelRepresented pi).app (op Z) w).val
   131	        = (abelDivAffTrans C (genus C)).app (op Z)
   132	            ((divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).toIso.hom.app (op Z) w.val) := fun _ => rfl
   133	  have hval : (abelDivAffTrans C (genus C)).app (op Z) sx
   134	      = (abelDivAffTrans C (genus C)).app (op Z) sy := by
   135	    have := congrArg Subtype.val h
   136	    rwa [happ, happ] at this
   137	  have habel : abelDivAff' C (genus C) Z sx = abelDivAff' C (genus C) Z sy := by
   138	    have := congrArg Subtype.val hval
   139	    rwa [abelDivAffTrans_app_coe, abelDivAffTrans_app_coe] at this
   140	  -- membership of the rank-one class of `sx`
   141	  have hmem : (abelDivAffTrans C (genus C)).app (op Z) sx
   142	      ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj (op Z) := x.property
   143	  -- arbitrary-test uniqueness forces the vehicle sections to agree
   144	  have hsxy : sx = sy := divFamZarAff_eq_of_rankOne pi Z sx sy hmem habel
   145	  exact Subtype.ext (hinj (hsx ▸ hsy ▸ hsxy))
   146	
   147	/-- Componentwise injectivity of the restricted represented Abel map on the big site: the
   148	`Σ`-extension preserves the slicewise injectivity of `rankOneAbelRepresented`. -/
   149	theorem rankOneAbelSigma_app_injective (Y : Schemeᵒᵖ) :
   150	    Function.Injective ((rankOneAbelSigma pi).app Y) := by
   151	  rintro ⟨a, ξ⟩ ⟨b, η⟩ h
   152	  have ha : (⟨a, (rankOneAbelRepresented pi).app (op (Over.mk a)) ξ⟩ :
   153	        Σ c : Y.unop ⟶ Spec (.of k),
   154	          (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor.obj (op (Over.mk c)))
   155	      = ⟨b, (rankOneAbelRepresented pi).app (op (Over.mk b)) η⟩ := h
   156	  obtain ⟨rfl, h2⟩ := Sigma.mk.inj_iff.mp ha
   157	  simp only [heq_eq_eq] at h2
   158	  obtain rfl := rankOneAbelRepresented_app_injective pi (Over.mk a) h2
   159	  rfl
   160	
   161	/-! ## The Abel inverse and the packaged iso -/
   162	
   163	namespace PicRankOneEvaluationDivisorData
   164	
   165	/-- **The Abel inverse law holds automatically**: every canonical evaluation-divisor classifier
   166	of the rank-one locus is a two-sided inverse of the restricted Abel map.  From the right inverse
   167	`E.divisor_abel` and injectivity of `rankOneAbelSigma pi`, the left inverse follows by
   168	cancellation. -/
   169	theorem abelInverse_of_uniqueness (E : PicRankOneEvaluationDivisorData pi) :
   170	    E.AbelInverse := by
   171	  have h : rankOneAbelSigma pi ≫ E.divisor
   172	      = 𝟙 (rankOneDivisorLocus (C := C) (pi := pi)) := by
   173	    ext Y d
   174	    change E.divisor.app Y ((rankOneAbelSigma pi).app Y d) = d
   175	    apply rankOneAbelSigma_app_injective pi Y
   176	    exact E.divisor_abel_app pi Y.unop ((rankOneAbelSigma pi).app Y d)
   177	  exact h
   178	
   179	/-- The rank-one family isomorphism, with the Abel inverse discharged: the restricted Abel map
   180	and the canonical evaluation divisor are mutually inverse on the big site. -/
   181	noncomputable def rankOneAbelIso (E : PicRankOneEvaluationDivisorData pi) :
   182	    rankOneDivisorLocus (C := C) (pi := pi) ≅ rankOneLocus (C := C) (pi := pi) :=
   183	  E.evaluationIso pi (E.abelInverse_of_uniqueness pi)
   184	
   185	end PicRankOneEvaluationDivisorData
   186	
   187	end
   188	
   189	end AlgebraicGeometry

     8	import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Subfunctor.Image
     9	
    10	/-!
    11	# The presentation locus for the rank-one Abel map
    12	
    13	`PicRankOneOpen` is the functorial locus in the degree-`genus C` Picard layer whose pullback to
    14	every affine test admits a tied `PicRankOneLocalPresentation`.  Quantifying after every affine
    15	pullback makes the condition intrinsic on arbitrary test schemes; stability under further
    16	pullback is exactly `picEtMap_comp`.
    17	
    18	The remaining declarations form the corresponding preimages in the widened divisor functor and
    19	in its canonical representing Yoneda functor, together with the restricted Abel transformations.
    20	These are logical subfunctors only.  In particular, this file does not assert that
    21	`PicRankOneOpen` is represented by an open subscheme.  The relative-openness acceptance gate and
    22	the conditional universal-divisor carrier contract are exposed separately in `DivRankOneOpen.lean`.
    23	-/
    24	
    25	set_option autoImplicit false
    26	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    27	
    28	universe u
    29	
    30	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
    31	
    32	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    33	
    34	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    35	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    36	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    37	variable (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi]
    38	
    39	noncomputable section
    40	
    41	/-- The rank-one presentation locus in the degree-`genus C` Picard layer.
    42	
    43	Membership means that every affine pullback of the input plus class admits a local presentation
    44	tied to that pullback.  This is the correct logical subfunctor underlying the future open Picard
    45	locus; no openness or representability assertion is part of this definition. -/
    46	def PicRankOneOpen :
    47	    Subfunctor (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)) where
    48	  obj T := {lam | ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    49	      (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),
    50	    Nonempty (PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi
    51	      ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op lam))}
    52	  map {T T'} f lam hlam A _ _ t := by
    53	    let F := picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)
    54	    have e : F.map t.op (F.map f lam) = F.map (t ≫ f.unop).op lam := by
    55	      apply Subtype.ext
    56	      exact (picEtMap_comp C f.unop t lam.1).symm
    57	    rw [e]
    58	    exact hlam A (t ≫ f.unop)
    59	
    60	/-! ## The public membership contract -/
    61	
    62	/-- The exact producer predicate for the rank-one locus.
    63	
    64	This is intentionally lambda-tied and quantifies over every affine pullback.  In particular, it
    65	is stronger than a field-fibre `h⁰ = 1`/`H¹ = 0` statement: a producer must supply the complete
    66	`PicRankOneLocalPresentation` structure for the pulled-back class. -/
    67	def PicRankOneOpen.LocalPresentationCondition
    68	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
    69	    (lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T) : Prop :=
    70	  ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    71	    (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),
    72	    Nonempty (PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi
    73	      ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op lam))
    74	
    75	/-- Unfolded membership in `PicRankOneOpen`, with the presentation tied to the pulled-back
    76	Picard class.  Keeping this predicate named is important for producers in later lanes: a
    77	field-level divisor or chart witness is not a substitute for this arbitrary-affine-pullback
    78	contract. -/
    79	theorem mem_picRankOneOpen_iff {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
    80	    (lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T) :
    81	    lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T ↔
    82	      ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    83	        (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),

    91	    {lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T}
    92	    (h : ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]

   107	/-- The inclusion of the public rank-one locus into its degree-genus ambient functor. -/
   108	def picRankOneOpenIncl :
   109	    (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor ⟶ picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ) :=
   110	  (PicRankOneOpen pi).ι
   111	
   112	/-- The same inclusion after the slice-to-big-site `Σ` extension.
   113	
   114	`IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` is a property of presheaves on schemes.  The rank-one functor is
   115	defined on the slice over `Spec k`, so the `Σ` extension is the category-correct carrier for the
   116	relative-open gate below. -/
   117	def picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl :
   118	    Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor ⟶
   119	      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)) :=
   120	  Over.sigmaExtensionNat (PicRankOneOpen pi).ι
   121	
   122	/-- Relative openness of the public locus, in Mathlib's presheaf sense.
   123	
   124	This is a named acceptance gate rather than an unproved global assertion.  A future geometric
   125	producer discharges it by supplying the represented open pullbacks; no arbitrary `Subfunctor` is
   126	silently treated as an open subscheme. -/
   127	def PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen : Prop :=
   128	  IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi)

   130	/-! ## The explicit fibre producer contract -/
   131	
   132	/-- A fibre of the rank-one locus over one test class, presented by an open of that test.
   133	
   134	The `exists_factor` field is tied to the displayed class `g` and to an arbitrary source value `v`.
   135	It is the family-level content needed for relative representability; the open immersion itself
   136	supplies uniqueness of the factor.  Thus this structure cannot be inhabited by an unrelated open
   137	or by a fieldwise dimension statement. -/
   138	structure PicRankOneOpen.FibrePresented
   139	    {X : Scheme.{u}}
   140	    (g : yoneda.obj X ⟶
   141	      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ))) where
   142	  W : X.Opens
   143	  fst : yoneda.obj (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶
   144	    Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor
   145	  sq : fst ≫ picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi = yoneda.map W.ι ≫ g
   146	  exists_factor : ∀ (S : Scheme.{u})
   147	    (v : (Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor).obj (Opposite.op S))
   148	    (w : S ⟶ X),
   149	    (picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi).app (Opposite.op S) v =
   150	      g.app (Opposite.op S) w →
   151	    ∃ u : S ⟶ (W : Scheme.{u}),
   152	      fst.app (Opposite.op S) u = v ∧ u ≫ W.ι = w
   153	
   154	namespace PicRankOneOpen.FibrePresented
   155	
   156	variable {X : Scheme.{u}}
   157	variable {g : yoneda.obj X ⟶
   158	  Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ))}
   159	
   160	/-- The fibre square supplied by `FibrePresented` is a pullback of presheaves. -/
   161	theorem isPullback (D : PicRankOneOpen.FibrePresented pi g) :
   162	    IsPullback D.fst (yoneda.map D.W.ι) (picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi) g := by
   163	  refine IsPullback.of_forall_isPullback_app fun S => ?_
   164	  rw [Types.isPullback_iff]
   165	  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
   166	  · exact congrArg (fun φ : yoneda.obj (D.W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶
   167	      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)) =>
   168	      φ.app S) D.sq
   169	  · rintro u₁ u₂ ⟨-, h₂⟩
   170	    exact (cancel_mono D.W.ι).mp h₂
   171	  · intro v w hvw
   172	    obtain ⟨u, hu₁, hu₂⟩ := D.exists_factor S.unop v w hvw
   173	    exact ⟨u, hu₁, hu₂⟩
   174	
   175	end PicRankOneOpen.FibrePresented
   176	
   177	/-- An arbitrary-test fibre producer discharges the relative openness gate. -/
   178	theorem picRankOneOpen_isOpen_of_fibrePresented
   179	    (D : ∀ (X : Scheme.{u})
   180	      (g : yoneda.obj X ⟶
   181	        Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ))),
   182	      PicRankOneOpen.FibrePresented pi g) :
   183	    PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen pi := by
   184	  refine MorphismProperty.relative.of_exists ?_
   185	  intro X g
   186	  let d := D X g
   187	  exact ⟨d.W, d.fst, d.W.ι, d.isPullback, inferInstance⟩
   188	
   189	/-- Expose a supplied relative-open certificate without hiding it behind typeclass search. -/
   190	theorem picRankOneOpen_isOpen_of_certificate
   191	    (h : PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen pi) : PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen pi :=
   192	  h
   193	
   194	/-- Extract the open immersion supplied by the relative-openness certificate on an arbitrary
   195	pullback.  This is the exact shape consumed by an eventual chart/fibre producer. -/
   196	theorem picRankOneOpen_openPullback
   197	    (h : PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen pi)
   198	    {X Z : Scheme.{u}}
   199	    (g : yoneda.obj X ⟶
   200	      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)))
   201	    (fst : yoneda.obj Z ⟶
   202	      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor)
   203	    (snd : Z ⟶ X)
   204	    (hpb : IsPullback fst (yoneda.map snd) (picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi) g) :
   205	    IsOpenImmersion snd :=
   206	  h.property g fst snd hpb
   207	
   208	/-- Pullback stability of the public rank-one locus, exposed independently of its definition. -/
   209	theorem picRankOneOpen_map_mem {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   210	    (f : T ⟶ T') {lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T}
   211	    (h : lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T) :
   212	    (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map f lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T' :=
   213	  (PicRankOneOpen pi).map f h
   214	
   215	/-- Pullback stability of the public locus, with the base-change direction made explicit. -/
   216	theorem picRankOneOpen_baseChange_mem {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   217	    (f : T ⟶ T') {lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T}
   218	    (h : lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T) :
   219	    (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map f lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T' :=
   220	  picRankOneOpen_map_mem pi f h

   222	/-- The inverse image of `PicRankOneOpen` under the affine widened Abel transformation.
   223

   225	open subscheme `DivRankOneOpen`. -/

   232	def divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter :
   233	    Subfunctor (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)) :=
   234	  (divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff pi).preimage
   235	    (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).toIso.hom

   238	def rankOneAbelAff :
   239	    (divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff pi).toFunctor ⟶
   240	      (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor :=
   241	  (PicRankOneOpen pi).fromPreimage (abelDivAffTrans C (genus C))

   243	/-- Restrict the canonical representation isomorphism to the rank-one presentation preimage. -/
   244	def rankOneRepresenterRestriction :
   245	    (divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi).toFunctor ⟶
   246	      (divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff pi).toFunctor :=
   247	  (divRankOnePresentationPreimageAff pi).fromPreimage
   248	    (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).toIso.hom

   251	def rankOneAbelRepresented :
   252	    (divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi).toFunctor ⟶

   259	theorem rankOneAbelRepresented_mem {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   260	    (x : (divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi).obj T) :

     9	/-!
    10	# The Jacobian challenge — statement file (with field base change)
    11	
    12	This is the single, self-contained **statement file** of the project: it collects every
    13	definition, instance, and theorem needed to *state* the main result, and nothing else. A reviewer
    14	reads this one file, compares it against the original challenge (`references/challenge.lean`, by
    15	Christian Merten) and its base-change extension, and is convinced the project formalizes the right
    16	thing. The genuinely-missing pieces are `sorry`; the base-change scaffolding (`baseChange`, the
    17	stability instances, `idIso`, `compIso`, and `Jacobian.congr` derived from `Jacobian.functor`) is
    18	genuinely proved here. Proofs of the `sorry`s live in the rest of the `AlgebraicJacobian/` tree and
    19	must not weaken or restate any signature below.
    20	
    21	By a **smooth curve** we mean a geometrically irreducible, smooth scheme of relative dimension one
    22	over a field, proper over that field.
    23	
    24	## Main definitions
    25	
    26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.genus` — genus of a proper, smooth curve.
    27	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian` — the Jacobian of a proper, smooth curve.
    28	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.ofCurve` — the Abel–Jacobi map associated to a `k`-rational point.
    29	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.functor` — functoriality of the Jacobian, bundled as a single
    30	  contravariant functor `(Curve k)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Grp (Over (Spec k))`.
    31	
    32	## Main theorems
    33	
    34	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus` — the Jacobian is smooth of relative
    35	  dimension `g = genus C`.
    36	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.exists_unique_ofCurve_comp` — the universal property: the Jacobian is
    37	  the Albanese variety of `C`.
    38	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.baseChangeIso` — the Jacobian commutes with base change of fields,
    39	  together with the identity/cocycle coherences (`baseChangeIso_id`, `baseChangeIso_comp`) and the
    40	  Abel–Jacobi compatibility `baseChange_ofCurve`.
    41	
    42	## Notes
    43	
    44	`noncomputable` is on the data-carrying declarations: their honest realizations rest on
    45	noncomputable Mathlib constructions. Names, argument types, and argument order are verbatim from
    46	the challenge; the `noncomputable` modifier is not a signature change.
    47	-/
    48	
    49	set_option autoImplicit false
    50	
    51	universe u
    52	
    53	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory MonObj
    54	
    55	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    56	
    57	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    58	  -- smooth curve
    59	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
    60	  -- proper
    61	  [IsProper C.hom]
    62	  -- geometrically irreducible
    63	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    64	
    65	/-- The category of smooth, proper, geometrically irreducible curves over `k`, with morphisms the
    66	morphisms of `k`-schemes. -/
    67	structure Curve (k : Type u) [Field k] where
    68	  /-- The underlying `k`-scheme. -/
    69	  carrier : Over (Spec (.of k))
    70	  [isProper : IsProper carrier.hom]
    71	  [smoothOfRelativeDimension : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 carrier.hom]
    72	  [geometricallyIrreducible : GeometricallyIrreducible carrier.hom]
    73	
    74	attribute [instance] Curve.isProper Curve.smoothOfRelativeDimension Curve.geometricallyIrreducible
    75	
    76	noncomputable instance (k : Type u) [Field k] : Category (Curve k) where
    77	  Hom X Y := X.carrier ⟶ Y.carrier
    78	  id X := 𝟙 X.carrier
    79	  comp f g := f ≫ g
    80	  id_comp := Category.id_comp
    81	  comp_id := Category.comp_id
    82	  assoc := Category.assoc
    83	
    84	-- data
    85	/-- The genus of a smooth proper curve: the `k`-dimension of the first cohomology group
    86	`H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` of the structure sheaf, viewed as a sheaf of `k`-modules on the small Zariski
    87	site of `C` (`Scheme.moduleKSheaf`), with cohomology the `Ext` from the constant sheaf
    88	(`CategoryTheory.Sheaf.HModule`). Finite-dimensionality of `H¹` is proved downstream. -/
    89	noncomputable def genus (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
    90	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] : ℕ :=
    91	  letI : C.left.Over (Spec (.of k)) := .ofHom C.hom
    92	  Module.finrank k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1)
    93	
    94	-- data
    95	/-- The Jacobian of a smooth, proper curve over a field `k`. -/
    96	noncomputable def Jacobian (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
    97	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
    98	    Over (Spec (.of k)) :=
    99	  sorry
   100	
   101	namespace Jacobian
   102	
   103	/-! ## The Jacobian of `C` is an abelian variety. -/
   104	
   105	-- data
   106	/-- The group scheme structure on the Jacobian of the curve `C`. -/
   107	noncomputable instance instGrpObj : GrpObj (Jacobian C) :=
   108	  sorry
   109	
   110	/-- The Jacobian of `C` is smooth of relative dimension `g` over `k`, where `g` is the
   111	genus of `C`. -/
   112	instance smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus : SmoothOfRelativeDimension (genus C) (Jacobian C).hom :=
   113	  sorry
   114	
   115	/-- The Jacobian of `C` is proper over `k`. -/
   116	instance : IsProper (Jacobian C).hom :=
   117	  sorry
   118	
   119	/-- The Jacobian of `C` is geometrically irreducible over `k`. -/
   120	instance : GeometricallyIrreducible (Jacobian C).hom :=
   121	  sorry
   122	
   123	/-- The Abel-Jacobi map from a smooth, proper curve to its Jacobian associated
   124	to a `k`-rational point of `C`. -/
   125	noncomputable def ofCurve (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) : C ⟶ Jacobian C :=
   126	  sorry
   127	
   128	/-- The Abel-Jacobi map sends the `k`-rational point `P` to `0`, where `0` (denoted by `η`) is the
   129	neutral element of the group scheme `Jacobian C`. -/
   130	theorem comp_ofCurve (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
   131	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   132	    (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) :
   133	    P ≫ ofCurve P = η[Jacobian C] :=
   134	  sorry
   135	
   136	/--
   137	The universal property of the Jacobian variety: For any abelian variety `A`, any morphism
   138	`f : C ⟶ A` with `f(P) = 0` factors uniquely through the Jacobian of `C`. In other words,
   139	`Jacobian C` is the Albanese variety of `C`.
   140	-/
   141	theorem exists_unique_ofCurve_comp (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
   142	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   143	    (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C)
   144	    {A : Over (Spec (.of k))} [Smooth A.hom] [IsProper A.hom] [GrpObj A]
   145	    [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom] (f : C ⟶ A) (hf : P ≫ f = η[A]) :
   146	    ∃! (g : Jacobian C ⟶ A), f = ofCurve P ≫ g :=
   147	  sorry
   148	
   149	/-- **Functoriality of the Jacobian**, bundled as a single contravariant functor: a curve goes to
   150	its Jacobian group scheme over `k`, and a morphism of curves to the pullback of line bundles. The
   151	functor laws (`map_id`, `map_comp`) are embedded in this `Functor`. The object action is pinned to
   152	the `Jacobian` above, so everything downstream stays phrased in terms of `Jacobian C`. -/
   153	noncomputable def functor (k : Type u) [Field k] :
   154	    (Curve k)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Grp (Over (Spec (.of k))) where
   155	  obj X := .mk (Jacobian X.unop.carrier)
   156	  map _ := sorry
   157	  map_id := sorry
   158	  map_comp := sorry
   159	
   160	end Jacobian

   162	/-! ## Base change of fields
   163	
   164	Base change of `k`-schemes along `k → L` sends `X` to `X ×_{Spec k} Spec L`. These definitions and
   165	the stability instances are genuine (no `sorry`); they set up the statements of the base-change
   166	compatibility of the Jacobian. -/
   167	
   168	/-- Base change of `k`-schemes along a field homomorphism `k → L`, i.e. `X ↦ X ×_{Spec k} Spec L`.
   169	-/
   170	noncomputable abbrev baseChange (k L : Type u) [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
   171	    Over (Spec (.of k)) ⥤ Over (Spec (.of L)) :=
   172	  Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L)))
   173	
   174	instance {k L : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   175	    [IsProper C.hom] : IsProper ((baseChange k L).obj C).hom :=
   176	  MorphismProperty.baseChange_obj (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L))) C inferInstance
   177	
   178	instance {k L : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   179	    [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] : GeometricallyIrreducible ((baseChange k L).obj C).hom :=
   180	  MorphismProperty.baseChange_obj (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L))) C inferInstance
   181	
   182	instance {k L : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   183	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] :
   184	    SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 ((baseChange k L).obj C).hom :=
   185	  have : MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChange (@SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1) :=
   186	    smoothOfRelativeDimension_isStableUnderBaseChange 1
   187	  MorphismProperty.baseChange_obj (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L))) C inferInstance
   188	
   189	-- The coherences mention curves of the form `(𝟭 _).obj C` and `(F ⋙ G).obj C`.
   190	instance {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom] :
   191	    IsProper ((𝟭 (Over (Spec (.of k)))).obj C).hom := ‹_›
   192	instance {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
   193	    GeometricallyIrreducible ((𝟭 (Over (Spec (.of k)))).obj C).hom := ‹_›
   194	instance {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] :
   195	    SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 ((𝟭 (Over (Spec (.of k)))).obj C).hom := ‹_›
   196	
   197	instance {k L M : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Field M] [Algebra k L] [Algebra L M]
   198	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom] :
   199	    IsProper ((baseChange k L ⋙ baseChange L M).obj C).hom :=
   200	  inferInstanceAs (IsProper ((baseChange L M).obj ((baseChange k L).obj C)).hom)
   201	instance {k L M : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Field M] [Algebra k L] [Algebra L M]
   202	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
   203	    GeometricallyIrreducible ((baseChange k L ⋙ baseChange L M).obj C).hom :=
   204	  inferInstanceAs (GeometricallyIrreducible ((baseChange L M).obj ((baseChange k L).obj C)).hom)
   205	instance {k L M : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Field M] [Algebra k L] [Algebra L M]
   206	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] :
   207	    SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 ((baseChange k L ⋙ baseChange L M).obj C).hom :=
   208	  inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 ((baseChange L M).obj ((baseChange k L).obj C)).hom)
   209	
   210	/-- Base change along `k → k` is the identity functor. -/
   211	noncomputable def baseChange.idIso (k : Type u) [Field k] :
   212	    baseChange k k ≅ 𝟭 (Over (Spec (.of k))) :=
   213	  eqToIso (by
   214	    change Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k))) = Over.pullback (𝟙 _)
   215	    rw [Algebra.algebraMap_self, CommRingCat.ofHom_id, Spec.map_id]) ≪≫ Over.pullbackId
   216	
   217	/-- Base change along a tower `k → L → M` is the composite of the two base changes. -/
   218	noncomputable def baseChange.compIso (k L M : Type u) [Field k] [Field L] [Field M]
   219	    [Algebra k L] [Algebra L M] [Algebra k M] [IsScalarTower k L M] :
   220	    baseChange k M ≅ baseChange k L ⋙ baseChange L M :=
   221	  eqToIso (by
   222	    change Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k M))) =
   223	      Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap L M)) ≫
   224	        Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L)))
   225	    rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp, ← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq]) ≪≫
   226	    Over.pullbackComp _ _
   227	
   228	namespace Jacobian
   229	
   230	/-- The Jacobian respects isomorphisms of curves — *derived* from the bundled functor
   231	`Jacobian.functor` via `Functor.mapIso`, not a primitive. Used to compare the two sides of the
   232	cocycle, whose curves agree only up to `baseChange.compIso`. -/
   233	noncomputable def congr {k : Type u} [Field k] {C C' : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   234	    [IsProper C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   235	    [IsProper C'.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C'.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C'.hom]
   236	    (e : C ≅ C') :
   237	    (.mk (Jacobian C) : Grp (Over (Spec (.of k)))) ≅ .mk (Jacobian C') :=
   238	  let j : (⟨C⟩ : Curve k) ≅ ⟨C'⟩ :=
   239	    { hom := e.hom, inv := e.inv, hom_inv_id := e.hom_inv_id, inv_hom_id := e.inv_hom_id }
   240	  (Jacobian.functor k).mapIso j.symm.op
   241	
   242	/-- **The base-change condition.** Jacobians commute with base change of fields: a canonical
   243	isomorphism `Jac(C)_L ≅ Jac(C_L)`, as group schemes over `L`. -/
   244	noncomputable def baseChangeIso (k L : Type u) [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L]
   245	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
   246	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
   247	    (baseChange k L).mapGrp.obj (.mk (Jacobian C)) ≅ .mk (Jacobian ((baseChange k L).obj C)) :=
   248	  sorry
   249	
   250	/-! ## Functoriality: the base change isomorphisms form a coherent system. -/
   251	
   252	/-- Identity coherence. -/
   253	theorem baseChangeIso_id (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
   254	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
   255	    baseChangeIso k k C =
   256	      (Functor.mapGrpNatIso (baseChange.idIso k)).app _
   257	        ≪≫ (Functor.mapGrpIdIso (C := Over (Spec (.of k)))).app _
   258	        ≪≫ Jacobian.congr ((baseChange.idIso k).app C).symm :=
   259	  sorry
   260	
   261	/-- Cocycle coherence for a tower `k → L → M`. -/
   262	theorem baseChangeIso_comp (k L M : Type u) [Field k] [Field L] [Field M]
   263	    [Algebra k L] [Algebra L M] [Algebra k M] [IsScalarTower k L M]
   264	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
   265	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
   266	    baseChangeIso k M C
   267	        ≪≫ Jacobian.congr ((baseChange.compIso k L M).app C) =
   268	      (Functor.mapGrpNatIso (baseChange.compIso k L M)).app _
   269	        ≪≫ (Functor.mapGrpCompIso (F := baseChange k L) (G := baseChange L M)).app _
   270	        ≪≫ (baseChange L M).mapGrp.mapIso (baseChangeIso k L C)
   271	        ≪≫ baseChangeIso L M ((baseChange k L).obj C) :=
   272	  sorry
   273	
   274	/-! ## Compatibility with the Abel-Jacobi map -/
   275	
   276	variable {L : Type u} [Field L] [Algebra k L]
   277	
   278	theorem baseChange_ofCurve (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
   279	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   280	    (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) :
   281	    (baseChange k L).map (ofCurve P) ≫ (baseChangeIso k L C).hom.hom.hom =
   282	      ofCurve (Functor.LaxMonoidal.ε (baseChange k L) ≫ (baseChange k L).map P) :=
   283	  sorry
   284	
   285	end Jacobian
   286	
   287	end AlgebraicGeometry

240	/-! ## Assembly of the stronger fibre datum -/
   241	
   242	/-- Assemble the public fibre presentation from the represented canonical evaluation-divisor
   243	square.  Its `exists_factor` field is derived from the pullback universal property. -/
   244	noncomputable def toFibrePresented_of_evaluationDivisorPullback
   245	    (F : PicRankOneFibrePresentationInput pi E g)
   246	    (hpb : F.EvaluationDivisorPullback) :
   247	    PicRankOneOpen.FibrePresented pi g where
   248	  W := F.W
   249	  fst := F.fst
   250	  sq := F.fst_comp_incl
   251	  exists_factor := by
   252	    simpa only [FibreFactorizationClause] using
   253	      F.fibreFactorizationClause_of_evaluationDivisorPullback pi hpb
   254	
   255	@[simp]
   256	lemma toFibrePresented_of_evaluationDivisorPullback_W
   257	    (F : PicRankOneFibrePresentationInput pi E g)
   258	    (hpb : F.EvaluationDivisorPullback) :

   264	    (hpb : F.EvaluationDivisorPullback) :
   265	    IsPullback F.fst (yoneda.map F.W.ι) (picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi) g :=
   266	  (F.toFibrePresented_of_evaluationDivisorPullback pi hpb).isPullback
   267

   270	theorem picRankOneOpen_isOpen_of_evaluationDivisorPullbackFamilies
   271	    (E : PicRankOneEvaluationDivisorData pi)
   272	    (D : ∀ (X : Scheme.{u})
   273	      (g : yoneda.obj X ⟶ rankOneAmbient (C := C)),
   274	      PicRankOneFibrePresentationInput pi E g)

     8	/-!
     9	# The Jacobian representability datum (Wave-4 seam D1, `JacobianData`)
    10	
    11	The pinned representability datum for the degree-zero étale-sheafified relative Picard
    12	functor `pic0Functor C` of the challenge curve: a representing object `J`, an honest
    13	`Functor.RepresentableBy` datum (no `Nonempty`, no choice), and the two construction
    14	certificates (`LocallyOfFiniteType`, `QuasiCompact`).  This is the frozen Wave-4
    15	interface shape (`informal/w4-datum-worksheet.md` §1.1, verbatim), together with the
    16	design-§5 consumers `grpObj` / `homEquiv` / `uniqueUpToIso` — and nothing else.
    17	
    18	## Ownership split (binding, w5-worksheet D1)
    19	
    20	* The **producer** `jacobianData C : JacobianData C`, the quasi-compactness certificate,
    21	  and the discharge of the frozen `Jacobian`/`instGrpObj` sorries of `Challenge.lean`
    22	  are **DAT-J property** (the parallel Wave-4 fleet).  None of them lives here.
    23	* This file is the **Wave-5/6/7 consumption interface**: downstream files take
    24	  `(d : JacobianData C)` as a section variable, activate the group structure per proof
    25	  via `letI := d.grpObj` (or `attribute [local instance] JacobianData.grpObj`), and
    26	  phrase every statement about `d.J`.  At DAT-J discharge time the frozen gate
    27	  instantiates them by `exact theorem_x … (jacobianData C)` — definitionally, since
    28	  `Jacobian C := (jacobianData C).J`.
    29	* Extensions to this file are **additive only**; the structure shape never changes.
    30	
    31	## The `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage
    32	
    33	`rep` is typed against `(pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat`
    34	so that mathlib's `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` applies **verbatim** with
    35	`F := pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat`.  The functor value at a test `T` is
    36	*definitionally* the coerced subgroup `↥(pic0Subgroup C T)`; `homEquiv` and
    37	`homEquiv_comp` below own this defeq once, exposing the equivalence against
    38	`pic0Subgroup C T` and the naturality against `pic0Map` — no consumer ever meets the
    39	`forget₂ ⋙ forget` spelling again.
    40	
    41	## η-defeq verdict (recon §5 "lower-order unknown", RECORDED)
    42	
    43	**POSITIVE, with one keying caveat.**  `Over.mk d.J.hom` is definitionally equal to
    44	`d.J` (structure-eta for `Comma`/`CostructuredArrow` plus unit-like eta for the
    45	`Discrete PUnit` right leg): the ascription
    46	`(d.grpObj : GrpObj (Over.mk d.J.hom))` elaborates as-is, so **no transport lemma is
    47	ever needed**.  Caveat: bare instance *search* does not unfold `Over.mk` on its own,
    48	so a consumer of `smooth_of_grpObj` — whose group hypothesis is `[GrpObj (Over.mk f)]`
    49	at `f := d.J.hom` — must key the instance at the `Over.mk` spelling:
    50	`letI : GrpObj (Over.mk d.J.hom) := d.grpObj` (pure defeq, zero cost; mathlib itself
    51	uses the same ascription idiom in `Group/Smooth.lean`).  Instances stated directly on
    52	`G : Over (Spec (.of K))` (e.g. `IsClosedImmersion η[G].left`) fire on `d.J` with no
    53	massage at all.  The `example`-level smoke tests at the bottom of this file are the
    54	machine-checked record; the T-chain (tangent lane) and S2 (`Smooth` via
    55	`smooth_of_grpObj`) may rely on this freely.
    56	
    57	## Main declarations
    58	
    59	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData C` — the frozen datum structure.
    60	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.grpObj` — the group-object structure on `d.J` via
    61	  `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` (the discharge route of the frozen `instGrpObj`).
    62	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.homEquiv` / `homEquiv_comp` — the universal property
    63	  in consumer form: `(T ⟶ d.J) ≃ pic0Subgroup C T`, natural against `pic0Map`.
    64	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.uniqueUpToIso` / `homEquiv_uniqueUpToIso_hom` — any
    65	  two data have canonically isomorphic representing objects (Wave-7's `baseChangeIso`
    66	  mechanism), with the intertwining property.
    67	-/
    68	
    69	set_option autoImplicit false
    70	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    71	
    72	universe u
    73	
    74	open CategoryTheory Opposite
    75	
    76	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    77	
    78	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
    79	
    80	/-- **The pinned representability datum** for the degree-zero étale-sheafified relative
    81	Picard functor of the curve `C` (w4-datum-worksheet §1.1, frozen).  Produced once, by
    82	explicit construction, in Wave 4 (DAT-J: `jacobianData`); consumed as a section
    83	variable everywhere else.  NEVER a sorried instance, NEVER `Nonempty` + choice.
    84	
    85	The typing of `rep` is chosen so that `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` applies verbatim with
    86	`F := pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat` (see `JacobianData.grpObj`). -/
    87	structure JacobianData (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    88	    [IsProper C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
    89	    Type (u + 1) where
    90	  /-- The representing object (the Jacobian-to-be). -/
    91	  J : Over (Spec (.of k))
    92	  /-- The pinned universal datum: `Hom(T, J) ≃ Pic⁰(T)`, naturally in the test `T`. -/
    93	  rep : ((pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat).RepresentableBy J
    94	  /-- Certificate from the construction (Kleiman 4.8(1) shape); NOT re-derived via the
    95	  EGA limit criterion. -/
    96	  locallyOfFiniteType : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom
    97	  /-- Certificate from the construction (a posteriori: `|J|` is the image of a
    98	  quasi-compact divisor scheme under the Abel map).  Feeds `IsProper` (Wave 5) via
    99	  `finite type = qc + lft`. -/
   100	  quasiCompact : QuasiCompact J.hom
   101	
   102	namespace JacobianData
   103	
   104	variable {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   105	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   106	
   107	/-- The group-object structure on the representing object, via mathlib's
   108	`GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` — this is the (definitional) discharge route of the frozen
   109	`Jacobian.instGrpObj`.  Not a global instance here (the datum is a section variable);
   110	activate per proof with `letI := d.grpObj` or
   111	`attribute [local instance] JacobianData.grpObj`. -/
   112	@[implicit_reducible]
   113	noncomputable def grpObj (d : JacobianData C) : GrpObj d.J :=
   114	  GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy d.J (pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) d.rep
   115	
   116	/-- **The universal property, consumer form**: morphisms into `d.J` are degree-zero
   117	étale Picard classes.  This accessor owns the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` defeq massage once:
   118	the target is the honest subgroup carrier `pic0Subgroup C T`. -/
   119	def homEquiv (d : JacobianData C) {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} :
   120	    (T ⟶ d.J) ≃ pic0Subgroup C T :=
   121	  d.rep.homEquiv
   122	
   123	/-- Naturality of `homEquiv` against the degree-zero restriction maps `pic0Map`
   124	(element form of the `RepresentableBy` naturality, with the functor value unfolded
   125	through `forget₂ ⋙ forget`). -/
   126	theorem homEquiv_comp (d : JacobianData C) {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   127	    (f : T' ⟶ T) (g : T ⟶ d.J) :
   128	    d.homEquiv (f ≫ g) = pic0Map C f (d.homEquiv g) :=
   129	  d.rep.homEquiv_comp f g
   130	
   131	/-- Representing objects are unique up to isomorphism (mathlib
   132	`Functor.RepresentableBy.uniqueUpToIso`): any two Jacobian data for the same curve have
   133	canonically isomorphic `J`.  This is Wave-7's `baseChangeIso` mechanism. -/
   134	noncomputable def uniqueUpToIso (d d' : JacobianData C) : d.J ≅ d'.J :=
   135	  d.rep.uniqueUpToIso d'.rep
   136	
   137	/-- The intertwining property of `uniqueUpToIso`: composing with the canonical
   138	isomorphism commutes with the two universal properties. -/
   139	theorem homEquiv_uniqueUpToIso_hom (d d' : JacobianData C) {T : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   140	    (f : T ⟶ d.J) :
   141	    d'.homEquiv (f ≫ (d.uniqueUpToIso d').hom) = d.homEquiv f := by
   142	  have h : (d.uniqueUpToIso d').hom = d'.rep.homEquiv.symm (d.rep.homEquiv (𝟙 d.J)) := rfl
   143	  rw [homEquiv, homEquiv, h, Functor.RepresentableBy.comp_homEquiv_symm]
   144	  exact (d'.rep.homEquiv.apply_symm_apply _).trans (d.rep.homEquiv_eq f).symm
   145	
   146	end JacobianData
   147	
   148	/-! ## η-defeq smoke tests (recon §5 lower-order unknown; `example`-level, nothing
   149	registered)
   150	
   151	The first test records that `Over.mk d.J.hom ≡ d.J` definitionally (structure eta); the
   152	second that instance resolution crosses it — `smooth_of_grpObj`'s hypothesis
   153	`[GrpObj (Over.mk f)]` at `f := d.J.hom` is discharged by `letI := d.grpObj`; the third
   154	that mathlib's `IsClosedImmersion η[d.J].left` instance fires on `d.J` as-is.  T-chain
   155	and S2 depend on these; if a mathlib bump ever breaks them, a transport lemma must be
   156	added HERE, not in the consumers. -/
   157	
   158	section EtaDefeqSmokeTests
   159	
   160	open MonObj
   161	
   162	variable {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   163	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   164	
   165	/-- Smoke test 1: `Over.mk d.J.hom` is definitionally `d.J` — the ascription
   166	elaborates with no transport. -/
   167	noncomputable example (d : JacobianData C) : GrpObj (Over.mk d.J.hom) := d.grpObj
   168	
   169	/-- Smoke test 2: `smooth_of_grpObj` applies to `d.J.hom` with no transport lemma;
   170	the group instance must be *keyed* at `Over.mk d.J.hom` (the ascribed `letI` below —
   171	instance search does not unfold `Over.mk` on its own, but the ascription is pure
   172	defeq). -/
   173	example (d : JacobianData C) [GeometricallyReduced d.J.hom] : Smooth d.J.hom :=
   174	  letI := d.locallyOfFiniteType
   175	  letI : GrpObj (Over.mk d.J.hom) := d.grpObj

   177	
   178	/-- Smoke test 3: the unit section of `d.J` is a closed immersion (mathlib's
   179	group-scheme instance fires on `d.J` directly, with the datum's group structure in
   180	scope). -/
   181	example (d : JacobianData C) [GrpObj d.J] : IsClosedImmersion η[d.J].left :=
   182	  inferInstance
   183	
   184	end EtaDefeqSmokeTests

     7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0SigmaSheaf
     8	
     9	/-!
    10	# Producing the Jacobian representability datum from a Zariski chart family
    11	
    12	The pinned datum `JacobianData C` of the curve `C` bundles a representing object for the
    13	degree-zero Picard functor together with the two finiteness certificates of that object.
    14	This file constructs it: first from a bare representation (`JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy`),
    15	and then — the substance — from a Zariski chart family of the Σ-extension sheaf, whose glued
    16	scheme is the representing object and whose charts carry the finiteness.
    17	
    18	## Main declarations
    19	
    20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy` — a representation of `pic0TypeFunctor C`
    21	  by `J`, plus `LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom` and `QuasiCompact J.hom`, is a `JacobianData C`.
    22	* `AlgebraicGeometry.gluedHom` / `AlgebraicGeometry.gluedOfCharts` — the glued scheme of a chart
    23	  family, placed over the base field by the Σ-component of the universal element of the
    24	  representation it induces.
    25	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartHom` — the structure morphism `X i ⟶ Spec k` of the `i`-th chart:
    26	  the Σ-component of the element of `pic0SigmaFunctor C` classified by `f i`.
    27	* `AlgebraicGeometry.toGlued_comp_gluedHom` — **the compatibility of the two**: the glue map
    28	  `X i ⟶ gluedOfCharts` composed with the structure morphism of the glued object is exactly
    29	  `chartHom i`.  So the charts are charts *over the base field*, and the glued object is
    30	  covered by them as a `k`-scheme.
    31	* `AlgebraicGeometry.locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom` — being locally of finite type is local
    32	  on the source, so it descends from the charts to the glued object.
    33	* `AlgebraicGeometry.quasiCompact_gluedHom` — over the affine base `Spec k`, quasi-compactness
    34	  of the glued object is compactness of its space, which a finite family of compact charts
    35	  supplies.
    36	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.ofCharts` — **the first producer of the Jacobian datum**:
    37	  a finite Zariski chart family of relatively representable open immersions into
    38	  `pic0SigmaSheaf C`, jointly locally surjective, with quasi-compact charts that are locally of
    39	  finite type over `k`, yields `JacobianData C`.
    40	
    41	## The hypothesis bundle
    42	
    43	Every declaration here carries exactly the three hypotheses of the frozen `Jacobian` of
    44	`Challenge.lean` — `IsProper`, `SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1`, `GeometricallyIrreducible`.  The
    45	`GeometricallyReduced C.hom` hypothesis of `Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean` is *not* an extra assumption:
    46	a morphism smooth of relative dimension `1` is smooth (`Smooth.of_smoothOfRelativeDimension_one`)
    47	and a smooth morphism is geometrically reduced (`Smooth.geometricallyReduced`), both global
    48	instances of `AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.GeometricallyReduced`, so instance resolution supplies it
    49	from the frozen bundle.  The `example` at the end of this file is the machine-checked record.
    50	-/
    51	
    52	set_option autoImplicit false
    53	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    54	
    55	universe u
    56	
    57	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
    58	
    59	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    60	
    61	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    62	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    63	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    64	
    65	/-! ## Packaging a representation as the datum -/
    66	
    67	/-- **Package a representation of the degree-zero Picard functor**, with its two finiteness
    68	certificates, as the pinned Jacobian datum.  The representation is stated in the
    69	`pic0TypeFunctor` spelling; that abbreviation unfolds to the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage that
    70	`JacobianData.rep` is typed against. -/
    71	noncomputable def JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    72	    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
    73	    (hlft : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom) (hqc : QuasiCompact J.hom) :
    74	    JacobianData C where
    75	  J := J
    76	  rep := rep
    77	  locallyOfFiniteType := hlft
    78	  quasiCompact := hqc
    79	
    80	@[simp]
    81	lemma JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy_J (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    82	    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
    83	    (hlft : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom) (hqc : QuasiCompact J.hom) :
    84	    (JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy C J rep hlft hqc).J = J :=
    85	  rfl
    86	
    87	@[simp]
    88	lemma JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy_rep (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    89	    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
    90	    (hlft : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom) (hqc : QuasiCompact J.hom) :
    91	    (JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy C J rep hlft hqc).rep = rep :=
    92	  rfl
    93	
    94	/-- The universal property of a packaged datum is the packaged representation. -/
    95	@[simp]
    96	lemma JacobianData.homEquiv_ofRepresentableBy (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))

   103	/-! ## The chart family and its glued object -/
   104	
   105	section Charts
   106	
   107	variable {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
   108	  (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
   109	
   110	/-- **The structure morphism of the `i`-th chart** over the base field: the Σ-component of the
   111	element of `pic0SigmaFunctor C` classified by `f i`.  A chart of the degree-zero Picard sheaf
   112	is by construction a scheme *together with* a map to `Spec k`, namely the base over which the
   113	line bundle it classifies lives; this is that map. -/
   114	noncomputable def chartHom (i : ι) : X i ⟶ Spec (.of k) := (yonedaEquiv (f i)).1
   115	
   116	variable (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i))
   117	variable [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)]
   118	
   119	/-- **The structure morphism of the glued object of a chart family**: mathlib's 01JJ engine
   120	glues the charts into a scheme representing the Σ-extension sheaf, and the Σ-component of the
   121	universal element of that representation is the map of that scheme to `Spec k`. -/
   122	noncomputable abbrev gluedHom :
   123	    (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued ⟶ Spec (.of k) :=
   124	  ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
   125	    (𝟙 (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued)).1
   126	
   127	/-- **The glued object of a chart family**, as a scheme over the base field.  This is the
   128	object represented by `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`. -/
   129	noncomputable abbrev gluedOfCharts : Over (Spec (.of k)) := Over.mk (gluedHom C f hf)
   130	
   131	/-- The universal element of the glued representation restricts along the `i`-th glue map to
   132	the element classified by `f i`. -/
   133	lemma representableBy_homEquiv_toGlued (i : ι) :
   134	    (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
   135	      (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.toGlued hf i) = yonedaEquiv (f i) :=
   136	  Scheme.LocalRepresentability.yonedaGluedToSheaf_app_toGlued hf
   137	
   138	/-- **The charts are charts over the base field**: the `i`-th glue map into the glued object,
   139	followed by the structure morphism of the glued object, is the structure morphism of the `i`-th
   140	chart.  Both sides are Σ-components of the same restriction of the universal element. -/
   141	lemma toGlued_comp_gluedHom (i : ι) :
   142	    Scheme.LocalRepresentability.toGlued hf i ≫ gluedHom C f hf = chartHom C f i := by
   143	  have h := congrArg Sigma.fst
   144	    ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv_eq
   145	      (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.toGlued hf i))
   146	  rw [representableBy_homEquiv_toGlued] at h
   147	  exact h.symm
   148	
   149	/-! ## The two finiteness certificates from the charts -/
   150	
   151	/-- **Locally of finite type descends from the charts**: the property is local on the source
   152	and the glue maps of the glue data cover the glued object, so if each chart is locally of finite
   153	type over the base field then so is the glued object. -/
   154	theorem locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i)) :
   155	    LocallyOfFiniteType (gluedHom C f hf) := by
   156	  refine IsZariskiLocalAtSource.of_openCover
   157	    (P := @LocallyOfFiniteType) (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).openCover fun i => ?_
   158	  have h := hlft i
   159	  rwa [← toGlued_comp_gluedHom C f hf i] at h
   160	
   161	/-- **Quasi-compactness descends from a finite family of quasi-compact charts**: the base
   162	`Spec k` is affine, so quasi-compactness of the structure morphism is compactness of the space
   163	of the glued object, and that space is the union of the finitely many compact chart images. -/
   164	theorem quasiCompact_gluedHom [Finite ι] (hcpt : ∀ i, CompactSpace (X i)) :
   165	    QuasiCompact (gluedHom C f hf) := by
   166	  haveI : Finite (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).openCover.I₀ := ‹Finite ι›
   167	  haveI : ∀ i, CompactSpace ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).openCover.X i) := hcpt
   168	  haveI : CompactSpace (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued :=
   169	    (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).openCover.compactSpace
   170	  exact HasAffineProperty.iff_of_isAffine.mpr ‹_›
   171	
   172	/-! ## The producer -/
   173	
   174	/-- **The first producer of the Jacobian datum**: a Zariski chart family of relatively
   175	representable open immersions into the Σ-extension sheaf of the degree-zero Picard functor,
   176	jointly locally surjective, indexed by a finite type, with quasi-compact charts that are locally
   177	of finite type over the base field, produces the pinned representability datum of the curve.
   178	
   179	The representing object is the glued scheme of the family, placed over `Spec k` by the
   180	Σ-component of the universal element; the two certificates are `locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom`
   181	and `quasiCompact_gluedHom`. -/
   182	noncomputable def JacobianData.ofCharts [Finite ι]
   183	    (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i))
   184	    (hcpt : ∀ i, CompactSpace (X i)) :
   185	    JacobianData C :=
   186	  JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy C (gluedOfCharts C f hf)
   187	    (pic0RepresentableByOfCharts C f hf)
   188	    (locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom C f hf hlft)
   189	    (quasiCompact_gluedHom C f hf hcpt)
   190	
   191	@[simp]
   192	lemma JacobianData.ofCharts_J [Finite ι]
   193	    (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i))
   194	    (hcpt : ∀ i, CompactSpace (X i)) :
   195	    (JacobianData.ofCharts C f hf hlft hcpt).J = gluedOfCharts C f hf :=
   196	  rfl
   197	
   198	/-- **The producer for an infinite atlas**: same as `JacobianData.ofCharts`, but the index type
   199	is arbitrary and quasi-compactness of the glued object is supplied directly instead of being
   200	derived from finitely many compact charts.
   201	
   202	This is the form the classical construction needs.  The charts of the degree-zero Picard functor
   203	are indexed by divisor *classes* — one chart per class whose twisted fibre class has an effective
   204	witness — and that index set is not finite; compactness of the glued object is then a genuine
   205	theorem about the Jacobian (it is the union of the images of a *quasi-compact* divisor scheme
   206	under the Abel map), not a consequence of finiteness of the atlas.  Note that the
   207	locally-of-finite-type certificate still descends from the charts with no finiteness hypothesis
   208	whatsoever: `locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom` never uses `Finite ι`. -/
   209	noncomputable def JacobianData.ofChartsOfCompactSpace
   210	    (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i))
   211	    (hcpt : CompactSpace (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued) :
   212	    JacobianData C :=
   213	  JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy C (gluedOfCharts C f hf)
   214	    (pic0RepresentableByOfCharts C f hf)
   215	    (locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom C f hf hlft)
   216	    (HasAffineProperty.iff_of_isAffine.mpr hcpt)
   217	
   218	@[simp]
   219	lemma JacobianData.ofChartsOfCompactSpace_J
   220	    (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i))
   221	    (hcpt : CompactSpace (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued) :
   222	    (JacobianData.ofChartsOfCompactSpace C f hf hlft hcpt).J = gluedOfCharts C f hf :=
   223	  rfl
   224	
   225	end Charts

   227	/-! ## The hypothesis bundle of the frozen `Jacobian` suffices
   228	
   229	`Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean` introduces `[GeometricallyReduced C.hom]` before its sheaf and
   230	representability statements, while the frozen `Jacobian` of `Challenge.lean` carries only
   231	`IsProper`, `SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1` and `GeometricallyIrreducible`.  There is no gap:
   232	geometric reducedness is *derived* from smoothness of relative dimension one by the global
   233	instances of `AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.GeometricallyReduced`, which is in the import closure of
   234	`Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean`.  Hence every declaration above elaborates under the frozen bundle alone,
   235	and the example below records it. -/
   236	
   237	example : GeometricallyReduced C.hom := inferInstance
   238	
   239	/-! ## What remains
   240	
   241	`JacobianData.ofCharts` reduces the frozen `Jacobian` of `Challenge.lean` — that is, the
   242	production of `jacobianData C : JacobianData C`, from which `Jacobian C := (jacobianData C).J` —
   243	to a single geometric statement about the degree-zero Picard sheaf of the curve, namely the
   244	existence of a finite Zariski atlas:
   245	
   246	> there exist a finite index type `ι`, schemes `X : ι → Scheme`, and morphisms of presheaves
   247	> `f i : yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ pic0SigmaFunctor C` such that
   248	>
   249	> 1. **(relative representability)** each `f i` is a relatively representable open immersion,
   250	>    `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i)`;
   251	> 2. **(coverage)** the family is jointly locally surjective for the big Zariski topology,
   252	>    `Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)`;
   253	> 3. **(chart finiteness)** each chart is locally of finite type over the base field with
   254	>    respect to its own structure morphism, `LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i)`, and each
   255	>    chart space is quasi-compact, `CompactSpace (X i)`.
   256	
   257	Nothing else about the Picard functor is needed: the sheaf condition is already discharged
   258	(`pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf`), the gluing is mathlib's (`Scheme.LocalRepresentability`), the
   259	Σ-descent to the slice is already discharged (`Functor.RepresentableBy.overSlice`), and the two
   260	certificates of the glued object are discharged here from (3).
   261	
   262	Conditions (1) and (2) are the geometric input — they are what the divisor-scheme/Abel-map
   263	machinery of the `DivScheme…` and `DivRep…` files exists to produce, one chart being carved out
   264	of a symmetric power of the curve by an effectivity locus.  Condition (3) is a property of those
   265	charts alone and does not interact with the Picard functor at all.
   266	
   267	If the atlas that machinery produces is *not* finitely indexed — and the classical one is not,
   268	its charts being indexed by divisor classes — then `JacobianData.ofChartsOfCompactSpace` is the
   269	form to use: `ι` is then arbitrary, condition (3) weakens to `LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i)`
   270	alone, and the second certificate becomes the single statement `CompactSpace` of the glued
   271	object.  That statement is not a bookkeeping hypothesis but a theorem about the Jacobian — the
   272	underlying space is the image of a quasi-compact divisor scheme under the Abel map — and it is
   273	where the quasi-compactness content of the construction actually lives. -/
   274	
   275	end AlgebraicGeometry
